name: sacral kingship

attributes.attribute: the idea that Celtic kingship was a sacred role, not only a political one
binds the king to rules and taboos known as buada and geis

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sacral kingship is a cosmological concept. The term holds that kingship was a sacred duty, not only a political office. Some writers use the phrase for Celtic kings. They claim the king brought good fortune through an honest reign. The idea stays controversial. The same term is used in non-Celtic settings, which clouds its meaning. Kings often came from royal blood. At other times a lesser man rose through divination by druids or through feats of arms. A ritual of inauguration raised him to power. The king then followed rules and taboos, such as buada and geis. Most scholars accept this view of Celtic rule. A minority claim kings were killed in hard times for the good of the land. That theory is widely discounted. Myths hint at such a fate, yet scholars say kings were driven out, not killed, when crops failed.
objective: Document sacral kingship as a cosmological concept.
